findings.claim: The page teaches that dict keys “must be immutable” and that “a tuple works.” Python actually requires keys to be hashable; a tuple is hashable only when all its elements are hashable. For example, hash(([1],)) raises TypeError. This matters to the objective of choosing a collection/key.
findings.recommendation: Replace the rule with “dict keys must be hashable.” State that strings, numbers, and tuples containing only hashable values work; lists and tuples containing a list do not. Keep the concrete city-pair quiz answer, whose strings make that tuple hashable.
